title:
Comment of Ethan Rubenstein in Docket(s)/Project(s) P-15424-000
Submission Date: 10/19/2026

documents.name: 151644.txt
documents.text:
Ethan Rubenstein, BRUNSWICK, ME.

Please reject the proposal from DeepGreen Western Passage SPV LLC for an 27 acre underwater data center within the Bay of Fundy — a vital feeding area, nursery, and migratory corridor for endangered species like North Atlantic right whales. DeepGreen has also identified a potential second phase that would expand the project to as much as 400 acres. Pollution, underwater noise, and more vessel traffic from this project put right whales, fin whales, sturgeon, and other marine species at risk. 

Data centers produce vast ongoing amounts of heat and thermal pollution. The Bay of Fundy and the Gulf of Maine are already two of the fastest warming bodies of water on the planet. The thermal pollution from an underwater data center would only increase this crisis and continue to degrade the habitat endangered species rely on. Such pollution from the DeepGreen project would also negatively impact fisheries in the area, causing harm to incomes of disadvantaged area residents and contribute to the decline of the natural resources that local fishing industries rely on, putting local livelihoods and economies at risk of irreversible harm.

Please reject this ill-advised and potentially catastrophic project.
